layout: Four columns. Rows: desktop idle, desktop typing, laptop idle, laptop typing. Unoccupied workstations use existing atlases.
prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create a production transparent pixel-art game sprite atlas from the two attached workstation atlases. Input 1 is the reference for the desktop workstation and seated man. Input 2 is the reference for the laptop workstation and seated woman. Primary change: make the fictional scam-office crew look like shady call-center operators through COSTUME AND PROPS: charcoal hood-up sweatshirt, dark trousers, visible over-ear headset with a small boom microphone, subtle teal screen light for the desktop worker; dark plum hoodie/jacket, black baseball cap, headset boom mic for the laptop worker. Keep their faces/hands natural and do not change skin tones or anatomy. A couple of tiny smartphones and a modest cash bundle on each desk help convey the fictional game role; no real scripts, logos, or readable text. Preserve warm amber pixel art, navy shadows, crisp dark outlines, wooden desk/beige CRT or laptop, chair, perspective, and original consistent scale. OUTPUT EXACTLY one square 4-COLUMN by 4-ROW grid of 16 equally spaced complete isolated workstation sprites. NO empty cells. Column orientations match the respective reference column orientations. Row 1: occupied DESKTOP, idle hands on keyboard. Row 2: exactly the SAME occupied DESKTOP sprites at exactly the same position and scale, alternate typing pose with only tiny hand and screen changes. Row 3: occupied LAPTOP with character correctly sitting IN the chair, hands on laptop keyboard. Row 4: exactly the SAME occupied LAPTOP sprites at exactly the same position and scale, alternate typing pose with only tiny hand and screen changes. All people complete head/torso/arms/legs seated facing monitor. Bottom of every workstation at the same relative position within each cell, centered, with uniform transparent gutters on all sides. Whole sprite kept inside its cell. Real alpha transparency outside sprites. No background, no grid lines, no labels, no cropped furniture, no oversized shadows. Prioritize exact matching between animation rows.

Precise-object-edit of this transparent 4x4 workstation atlas. Preserve top TWO rows (desktop) exactly. Repair ONLY the bottom two rows (laptop), maintaining exact 4 columns, 4 rows, square canvas, same sizes and anchors. Row 3 column 4 is missing its person: add a COMPLETE visible woman seated centered IN that black chair with her torso and head in front of the chair backrest, hands at the laptop keyboard, wearing dark plum jacket, black baseball cap and black call-center headset with microphone, like row 3 columns 1-3. Keep every laptop oriented toward the person, with screen facing her. Now make row 4 the exact corresponding animation version of row 3: SAME woman with SAME black cap, headset, clothing, same complete silhouette and sitting position, identical desk/computer/chair/cash/phones in each column. Only change fingers by 1-2 pixels and tiny screen lights between row 3 and 4. Do not use a bare-haired or bun-only version in row 4. Each of the eight laptop cells MUST contain one complete seated person, correct head/torso/hips/legs, with no missing body parts. Restore the character even when partly occluded, with visible head and torso above chair. Do not move workstations or change transparent margins. Preserve actual alpha transparency, pixel art style, all 16 cells, no text.
